question: Who is Osei Tweneboah and what does he research? Is it data science or more pure math?
answer:
Osei Tweneboah is an Associate Professor of Data Science in the School of Science, Nursing, and Health. [6] His talk, “Can We Predict Which Students Won’t Show Up? A Data Science Approach to College Enrollment,” explores “summer melt”—students who commit to enroll but do not show up. It uses real admissions data and machine-learning techniques to identify students at risk of not enrolling, focusing on how data-driven insights can support institutional decisions, student engagement, and enrollment outcomes. [8]

The work described is applied data science, not pure mathematics: the page explicitly describes it as a data science approach to a real-world education problem. It does not describe this research as pure math. [8]

Contact: otwenebo@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7332; office ASB-411. Office hours: “In-person or Virtual. Thur. 11am-1pm; Fri. 10am-11am or by Appointment.” [6]

Sources: [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/snh/faculty/osei-tweneboah/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/research-and-scholarship/faculty-scholarship-symposium-series/)
